title: Wipro Exits Nifty 50 for the First Time as BSE Takes Its Spot
excerpt: The NSE's semi-annual index review replaces the struggling IT giant with exchange operator BSE, reflecting the shifting landscape of Indian technology.
body:
• BSE Ltd will replace Wipro in the Nifty 50 index effective September 30, 2026, following NSE's semi-annual review
  • BSE's average free-float market cap of ₹1.41 lakh crore dwarfed Wipro's ₹55,930 crore, triggering the swap
  • Wipro is down 29.5% in 2026 and has been dropped from the benchmark for the first time since its brief 2013 exit during a demerger
  • The reshuffle will force index-tracking funds managing billions to rebalance their portfolios before September 30

Wipro Ltd is being removed from India's benchmark Nifty 50 index, replaced by exchange operator BSE Ltd in a swap that takes effect September 30. The move, announced by NSE Indices during its semi-annual review on August 11, marks the starkest signal yet of the shifting fortunes within India's IT services sector.

Why BSE Got In and Wipro Got Out

The decision came down to numbers. BSE's average free-float market capitalisation over the six-month review period stood at ₹1,40,879 crore — more than 2.5 times Wipro's ₹55,930 crore. Under NSE rules, an incoming stock must have an average free-float market cap at least 1.5 times that of the smallest constituent being removed. BSE cleared that bar comfortably.

Wipro will move to the Nifty Next 50, joining Hitachi Energy India, Polycab India, Vedanta Aluminium Metal, and Vodafone Idea. BSE also enters the Nifty 100, replacing Indian Hotels Company, Lodha Developers, REC, Shree Cement, and United Spirits.

A Historic Exit for Indian IT

This is effectively the first real removal of Wipro from the Nifty 50 since the benchmark was launched. The company had a brief exit between April and September 2013, but that was a technical consequence of its non-IT business demerger, not a reflection of declining market standing.

This time, the removal reflects genuine erosion. Wipro's stock is down 29.5% in 2026, making it the worst performer on the Nifty IT index. The company missed analyst estimates for its June-quarter results and guided September-quarter revenue between a 1.5% decline and 0.5% growth in constant-currency terms.

"Wipro has always had a growth problem. Even now, if you adjust for acquisitions, organic growth was about negative 2% quarter-on-quarter. Growth has been elusive."

— Sushovan Nayak, Lead Analyst, Anand Rathi Institutional Equities

Total deal wins fell to $3.37 billion from $5 billion a year earlier. Fourteen brokerages cut their price targets on Wipro after the most recent quarter, dragging the median target to ₹187 from ₹210.

What's Behind Wipro's Slide

Wipro's troubles mirror broader headwinds facing India's $315 billion IT services sector — subdued client spending, prolonged decision-making cycles, and AI-driven efficiency measures that are reducing the volume of traditional outsourcing work. But while rivals like TCS, HCLTech, and Tech Mahindra have shown greater resilience, analysts say Wipro has struggled to convert large contract wins into actual revenue growth.

Ambit Capital warned that fiscal 2027 could mark the fourth straight year of revenue decline for Wipro, setting it apart from its top-tier peers.

What the Rebalancing Means for Investors

The index swap will trigger mechanical portfolio adjustments. Every fund that tracks the Nifty 50 — ETFs, index funds, and passive portfolios managing billions — must sell Wipro and buy BSE before the September 30 effective date. That creates predictable selling pressure on Wipro and buying pressure on BSE in the weeks ahead.

BSE, whose stock is up 37% in 2026, also benefits from the timing. The National Stock Exchange is preparing for what could be one of the largest IPOs in Indian history, and it would likely list exclusively on BSE — the very company NSE just elevated into its own flagship index.
